name: empty-uri-permitted-allows-anything-invalid
description: An empty-IA5String uniformResourceIdentifier permitted subtree. RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 does not normatively specify what an empty URI constraint base means, and implementations diverge: Go's uriConstraints delegates the host part to dnsConstraints.all and accepts every URI; OpenSSL's nc_uri has no empty-base short-circuit (the 'Empty matches everything' line is only in nc_dns), so an empty permitted URI base matches no real URI and OpenSSL rejects the chain as a permitted-subtree violation. The verdict here is contested - the file is labeled invalid only to match the stricter (OpenSSL) reading; treat the inter-validator divergence as the load-bearing observation.
references: Go src/crypto/x509/constraints.go uriConstraints (delegates host part to dnsConstraints.all)
OpenSSL crypto/x509/v3_ncons.c nc_uri (no 'Empty matches everything' branch)
notes: Go: newDNSConstraints sees the zero-length URI host and sets dnsConstraints.all = true; the leaf URI matches the permitted subtree and the chain is accepted.
OpenSSL: nc_uri compares the leaf URI's host against the constraint string; an empty constraint matches no host, so the leaf falls outside permittedSubtrees and the chain is rejected.
GnuTLS: accepts. As with check_dns_constraints, an empty permitted entry is treated as 'not a permit' and skipped; with no other permitted URI entries the chain falls through to accept.
